text:
Iris: Thanks for the runtime deep-dive. Couple of pointed Qs for the roadmap doc and canary playbook: 

- Microbatching: what are safe defaults for ultra-low-latency chat routes vs high-throughput embedding jobs? Any guidance on dynamic switching?
- KV cache: do we guarantee per-session isolation for multi-tenant routes or rely on namespacing + best-effort shared prefixes? Any risk of stale context showing up in convo threads?
- Kernel rollout: who schedules kernel canaries, what telemetry gates do we use, and who has emergency revert rights?
- Product asks: one short dashboard (PM-friendly) — what three signals should it show?

Ben: Quick answers from runtime lead: 
- Microbatching defaults: chat routes default max_batch=4 (latency-first) with aggressive microbatch flush (100ms); mid-latency chat can use 8. Throughput/embeddings default 64 (or 128 on A100). We support route-level dynamic policies (route hints + traffic fraction) but switching is infra-controlled today.

Kavita: KV cache semantics: strict namespacing per-tenant and per-session key prefixes. We pin a session's prefix for the first 120–300s to avoid early eviction; after that we allow best-effort shared prefix caching for cost savings. Cache is advisory — never rely on it for correctness. Stale context risk is low if you key by session_id; don't mix session-less keys.

Luis: Kernel rollout + gates: runtime eng schedules canaries (default 5% traffic / 20–30m). Gates we monitor: p95 token-latency, overall request success rate, and OOM/GC spikes. Automated fallback routes to a compatible quantized variant if latency breach persists for 30s. Emergency revert authority sits with SRE (on-call) — they can force partial drain + rollback. Normal rollbacks happen automatically if error rate > 0.8% for the canary window.

Iris: Product dashboard guidance?

Ben: Keep it to three curves: p50/p95 token-latency (single graph), request success rate (errors per minute), and cost per 1k tokens (or cost per 1000 reqs). Add model-variant traffic split as a small pie chart if PMs want rollout visibility.

Kavita: Quick perf snapshot (staging pool zeta, single-token conts):
- chat batch=4 -> p50 9ms, p95 28ms, p99 85ms
- chat batch=8 -> p50 12ms, p95 56ms, p99 190ms
- embeddings batch=128 -> p50 190ms, p95 640ms
Note: we saw a 10% p99 improvement when prewarm is enabled for long-context routes.

Luis: Minimal canary snippet for roadmap doc: 
```
canary:
  traffic_fraction: 0.05
  duration_minutes: 30
  trace_sample_rate: 1.0
  gates:
    - p95_token_latency_ms: 200
    - error_rate_pct: 0.8
  fallback_variant: quantized-stable
```

OpsBot: Canary scheduled: canary/2301234567 at 2026-05-02T15:00:00Z. Alerts: runtime-canary-latency, runtime-canary-oom, runtime-canary-errors.

Iris: Thanks — Ben/Kavita please drop the staging dashboard link and I'll fold this into the all-hands notes. Also collecting 3 representative prompts for prewarm tests: 1 short convo, 1 long context (~1500 tokens), 1 embedding batch.

Ben: staging dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/zeta/runtime-batching-staging (has histograms + mem traces).

Kavita: test prompts: short: "Summarize today's meeting in one line." long: 1500-token policy doc fragment (repeat noise allowed) embeddings: 128 small JSON docs.

Iris: Perfect. I'll add the links + canary snippet to the roadmap doc and tag runtime + SRE for the tabletop. Closing this follow-up; will ping when notes are live. :sparkles:
